title: 3. Distribution, Supply Chain & Unit Economics
subtitle: OEM zero-base pricing, captive foundry integration, working-capital compression, and the FY2026 ₹100 waterfall

web_blocks.html: ZF Steering Gear sells roughly 90% of its automotive steering output directly to Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) and only about 10% through the replacement aftermarket [8]. Direct OEM supply creates predictable multi-year platform volumes. This occurs because commercial vehicle makers rarely re-validate safety-critical steering assemblies once a truck model enters production. The trade-off is pricing power. Large OEMs negotiate under zero-base costing and annual productivity-giveback clauses, forcing ZF Steering to absorb part of steel, alloy. Wage inflation unless it extracts internal manufacturing efficiencies [8].

That margin squeeze explains why management committed ₹140–150 crore across FY2024–FY2027 to backward integration [3][8]. Previously, the company bought rough SG iron housings and aluminium components from external vendors, paying outside foundry margins and carrying buffer inventory. By commissioning Metacast Auto in Kolhapur for precision SG iron and cast iron housings and scaling DriveSys in Supa for machined aluminium components and extrusions, management aims to capture vendor margins in-house and shorten lead times [12][17]. Early evidence appears in working capital. Net working capital days compressed sharply from 103 days in FY2022 and 66 days in FY2024 down to 21 days in FY2026, driven by payable days stretching from 40 to 61 and debtor days tightening from 82 to 64 [1].

web_blocks.html: The FY2026 waterfall exposes the central unit-economic paradox of ZF Steering Gear. Cash generation at the factory level is healthy. ₹98 crore of operating cash flow on ₹75 crore of EBITDA (a 131% conversion ratio, or 145% on a pre-tax basis proves that customers pay on time and inventory is under control [1]). Yet accounting profit was compressed to ₹12 crore (just ₹2.10 per ₹100 of sales because depreciation absorbed ₹47 crore—more than 8% of revenue—and the effective tax rate hit 58% as profitable parent earnings could not immediately offset subsidiary tax friction [1]. Meanwhile, ₹109 crore of capital spending outstripped operating cash flow, leaving free cash flow at -₹11 crore [1].

For an owner, this means the business has strong working-capital velocity but heavy capital intensity during its build-out phase. Until Supa and Kolhapur finish their capex cycle and grow into their depreciation base, free cash flow will remain tight. Next, we test how durable the company's competitive moat really is against domestic rivals and global technology shifts.

From a unit-economics standpoint, the FY2026 consolidated waterfall highlights a sharp divergence between working-capital efficiency and capital-expenditure intensity [8]. On ₹571 Cr of revenue, operating profit reached ₹75 Cr (13.1% OPM) and working-capital days compressed to 21 days, enabling ₹98 Cr of cash flow from operations [8]. Yet ₹109 Cr of fixed-asset additions absorbed every rupee of operating cash, leaving consolidated free cash flow at -₹11 Cr [8].

Evaluating supply-chain resilience shows that Metacast Auto Pvt Ltd (Kolhapur) provides critical backward integration in precision SG-iron and grey-iron castings, reducing reliance on third-party foundries during peak OEM demand [11]. Combined with DriveSys's in-house billet casting at Supa, ZF Steering Gear controls more of its upstream metallurgy than typical small-cap auto-ancillary assemblers [5, 11].

Examining conversion costs reveals that power, fuel, and subcontracting charges sit alongside employee costs (~11%–13% of sales) as key operating-leverage levers [8]. As DriveSys extrusion volumes scale, energy efficiency per metric tonne of anodised aluminium and scrap-recovery rates on billet casting directly determine whether consolidated EBITDA margins can sustain 13%–14% across the cycle [5, 8].

Because alloy steel, pig iron. Primary aluminium represent the bulk of raw material input costs, quarterly gross-margin stability depends on timely OEM indexation pass-throughs and DriveSys scrap-recovery discipline [5, 8].

Tight working-capital control remains a clear operational strength. Cutting net working capital to 20.6 days freed up ₹98 Cr of operating cash flow in FY26. Lower capex is now the missing link for free cash flow.

epigraph.quote: A factory can convert 130 percent of its EBITDA into operating cash and still burn cash overall if its capital-expenditure appetite outruns its depreciation shield.
epigraph.author: Pass 1 Forensic Principle

book_paragraphs: Walk through the supply chain of ZF Steering Gear and you immediately see two forces pulling in opposite directions. On the demand side, roughly 90% of its steering systems ship straight to commercial vehicle and tractor factories, with only 10% going to the replacement aftermarket. Selling directly to Tata Motors, Ashok Leyland, or Mahindra gives the company steady multi-year volume once a truck model is launched, because no OEM wants to re-test a safety-critical steering box mid-cycle. The catch is that big truck makers use zero-base costing, meaning they audit your material bills and demand annual price givebacks. You cannot pass through cost inflation automatically.

To protect its margins under that pressure, management launched a ₹140 to ₹150 crore backward-integration drive across Kolhapur and Supa. By casting iron housings at Metacast Auto and extruding aluminium parts at DriveSys, the company is trying to keep supplier markups inside the group. At the same time, it tightened its working capital dramatically—cutting net working capital from 103 days in FY2022 and 66 days in FY2024 down to just 21 days in FY2026. Customers paid faster, inventory moved quicker, and supplier credit stretched from 40 days to 61 days.

Now look at what happened to every ₹100 of revenue in FY2026. Out of ₹571 crore in consolidated sales, operating expenses took ₹496 crore, leaving ₹75 crore in EBITDA—about ₹13.13 per ₹100. Because working capital freed up cash, operating cash flow actually hit ₹98 crore, or ₹17.16 per ₹100. On the surface, that looks like a cash machine.

Yet follow that ₹100 down to the bottom line and the picture changes. Depreciation swallowed ₹47 crore—₹8.23 out of every ₹100—because the new Supa and Kolhapur assets are heavy on the balance sheet. Interest took ₹8 crore, taxes took ₹17 crore at an elevated 58% effective rate, and reported net profit shrank to just ₹12 crore, or ₹2.10 per ₹100. Worse, capital spending hit ₹109 crore during the year, leaving free cash flow negative at -₹11 crore. That is the core unit-economic tension you have to watch: operations generate cash efficiently, but heavy capital spending is still eating every rupee of it.
Once capital expenditure steps down from ₹109 Cr toward ₹30 Cr maintenance levels, that 20.6-day working-capital discipline can finally shine through in positive free cash flow.

book_subsections.title: Direct OEM Supply vs. Aftermarket Replacement
paragraphs: Unlike consumer goods companies that spend heavily on television ads and distributor margins, ZF Steering Gear sells primarily through direct engineering-to-engineering contracts with OEMs [1, 4]. Its sales team consists of application engineers who sit with truck and tractor chassis designers two to three years before a vehicle platform launches.

Once a model enters production, deliveries operate on just-in-time schedules from Pune, Pithampur, and Supa directly to OEM assembly plants. Aftermarket replacement demand—servicing older trucks and buses across India's highway corridors—provides a higher-margin, steadier tail when new truck sales slow down, though OEM volumes still dominate revenue.

On the raw material side, alloy steel bars, precision forgings, and aluminium ingots represent the largest cost buckets. Most OEM contracts include quarterly or semi-annual raw-material pass-through clauses, which protect gross margins from sudden commodity spikes, though timing lags of one to two quarters can briefly pinch quarterly profitability.

book_subsections.title: Reading the ₹100 Revenue-to-Free-Cash-Flow Waterfall
paragraphs: Let us trace every ₹100 of consolidated revenue earned in FY2026 through the cash register [8]. Roughly ₹86.87 went out the door to cover raw materials, employee wages, power, and plant overheads, leaving ₹13.13 of operating profit before depreciation.

Thanks to tight working-capital discipline—receivables, inventory, and payables netted down to just 21 days from 66 days two years earlier—cash flow from operations actually came in at ₹17.16 per ₹100 of sales, or ₹98 Cr in total [8]. That is a remarkable operational achievement.

Why, then, was there no cash left over for dividends? Because for every ₹100 of revenue, management reinvested ₹19.09 (₹109 Cr) into new plants and machinery [8]. Until that capex wave finishes and maintenance spending drops toward ₹4–₹5 per ₹100 of sales, free cash flow remains negative.

book_subsections.title: Working Capital Discipline: The Quiet Bright Spot
paragraphs: In Indian small-cap manufacturing, working capital is usually where optimistic growth stories go to die. Companies report booming sales on paper while receivables balloon past 120 days and cash never hits the bank.

That is why the drop in ZF Steering Gear's working-capital cycle from 103 days in FY22 to 20.6 days in FY26 stands out so sharply [8]. Management tightened receivables and inventory turns even while scaling consolidated revenue past ₹570 Cr.
For you as a shareholder, that 21-day cash cycle is the single strongest piece of evidence that Q2 FY27's revenue surge represents genuine customer demand rather than aggressive channel stuffing.

book_subsections.title: Where Every Rupee of Cost Goes Inside the Plant
paragraphs: When you walk an extrusion and machining plant, two invisible numbers govern unit economics: scrap rate and machine uptime. In aluminium billet casting and extrusion, every percentage point of trim scrap that has to be remelted costs electricity and furnace time.

Similarly, in precision steering gear machining, tool wear and rejection rates on worm shafts and piston racks determine whether a batch is profitable. Because Metacast Auto supplies castings in-house and DriveSys casts its own billets, management has tighter control over input quality than an assembler buying finished blanks [5, 11].

Keep an eye on gross margins and other expenses in upcoming quarterly filings: if raw-material-to-sales stays stable while employee and other expenses drop as a percentage of revenue, operating leverage is working in your favour.

book_subsections.title: Managing Commodity Swings Inside OEM Contracts
paragraphs: Investors often worry that rising steel or aluminium prices will crush an auto-component supplier's margins overnight. In practice, Tier-1 OEM contracts reset raw material benchmarks every quarter or two.
The real risk is a sharp one-quarter timing mismatch during a sudden commodity spike, or a prolonged slump in capacity utilization where fixed depreciation cannot be spread across enough units.

book_subsections.title: Why Cash Conversion Matters More Than Margin Percentages
paragraphs: Many manufacturing companies report attractive EBITDA margins on paper only to trap that profit inside slow-moving inventory and overdue customer receivables. At ZF Steering Gear, compressing net working capital down to 20.6 days proves that customers are paying on time and inventory is turning briskly [8].

Once capital expenditure moderates from its ₹109 Cr peak back toward maintenance levels, that tight working-capital discipline will allow operating cash flow to convert cleanly into free cash flow [8].

book_subsections.title: Why Working Capital Turns Matter So Much
paragraphs: In industrial supply chains, fast-growing subsidiaries often soak up cash in unpaid customer invoices and bloated raw-material yards. That is why ZF Steering Gear's compression of net working capital down to 20.6 days is such an encouraging operational signal.

If management keeps that 21-day cash conversion cycle intact while stepping capital expenditure down from ₹109 Cr toward maintenance levels, operating cash flow will quickly convert into distributable free cash flow.
